pathway.title: Allison Transmission Holdings Inc — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The legacy transmission franchise is the main support and held its margin through a down year. Allison Transmission earned an adjusted EBITDA margin of 37.47% in the nine months, and in 2025 net sales fell 6.67% while adjusted EBITDA fell only 3.00%, lifting the margin from 36.12% to 37.54%. Long-term agreements cover over 90% of North American on-highway unit volume and service parts, support equipment and other sales were 21% of 2025 revenue, so contracted volumes and replacement demand cushion a mild downturn. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 80; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation MG-1; calculation MG-2; calculation MG-3; calculation MG-4; calculation MG-5

Leverage is higher and the improvement so far is partly arithmetic. Total debt to reported EBITDA was 4.23x at 2026-03-31 and 3.31x at 2026-09-30, against 2.83x at year-end 2025, with debt down USD 255 million over the two quarters and last-twelve-months EBITDA rising as acquired quarters replaced pre-closing ones. On the issuer's adjusted measure net debt is 2.46x EBITDA, so true leverage may be lower than the reported ratio suggests, although no pro forma figure confirms that. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation LV-1; calculation LV-2; calculation LV-3; calculation LV-7; calculation LV-8

Interest cover is the weakest financial metric and will not recover quickly. EBITDA covered cash interest 6.55x over the last twelve months against 8.50x in 2025, and net interest expense of USD 51 million in the third quarter annualises to USD 204 million, which puts run-rate cover at 5.94x. The USD 1,699 million of floating-rate term debt has no swaps, so each 1% rise in rates adds USD 16.99 million of interest. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 101; calculation CV-1; calculation CV-2; calculation CV-3; calculation CV-4; calculation CV-6; calculation CV-7

Liquidity is adequate but thin in the United States, and maturities are distant. Liquidity is USD 1,493 million, but USD 361 million of the USD 497 million of cash is held by foreign subsidiaries, leaving USD 136 million of domestic cash behind the revolver. Only USD 320 million falls due through 2027 and 78.29% of principal matures in 2031 or later, so refinancing is a medium-term rather than a near-term test. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation LQ-1; calculation LQ-2; calculation LQ-3; calculation LQ-4

Noteholders now sit behind more secured debt. Secured term debt rose by USD 1,190 million to USD 1,699 million, 42.49% of principal, ahead of USD 2,300 million of unsecured notes, so the existing notes carry more priority claims while the debt documents that would size collateral and permitted debt are not supplied. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 101; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation CS-1; calculation CS-2; calculation CS-3; calculation CS-4

Off-Highway is the unproven part of the credit. It earns an adjusted EBITDA margin of 14.03% against 37.47% for Allison Transmission on 45.10% of nine-month sales, implied pro forma sales growth is 7.57%, the issuer calls agriculture and industrial demand subdued, and goodwill and intangibles of USD 1,645 million are 62.60% of the price. Weak margins would slow deleveraging and invite impairment. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 8; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation MG-6; calculation MG-9; calculation MG-12; calculation CS-8; calculation CS-9

Financial policy is the main judgement call. The issuer returned USD 195 million to shareholders in nine months, 29.46% of free cash flow, while repaying USD 410 million of debt, and its net leverage target of 2.0x has no definition or date. Creditors therefore depend on management's discretion for the pace of deleveraging. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-05-04_d138525dex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation FC-4; calculation FC-5; calculation FC-6

cells.text: World’s largest maker of fully automatic transmissions for medium- and heavy-duty commercial vehicles and for medium and heavy tactical U.S. defense vehicles; since 2026-01-01 also a provider of off-highway drivetrain and motion solutions
Two reportable segments from Q1 2026: Allison Transmission and Allison Off-Highway Drive & Motion Systems; one segment before
North America on-highway 51%, outside North America on-highway 17%, global off-highway 2%, defense 9%, service parts, support equipment and other 21%; the year excludes the acquired business
Allison Transmission 2,474 and Allison Off-Highway 2,032 of 4,506 net sales (45.10% Off-Highway)
Top five OEM customers were about 52% of FY2025 net sales; Daimler AG 18%, PACCAR Inc. 11%, Traton SE 10%; the combined group’s concentration is not supplied
OEM customers representing over 90% of North American on-highway unit volume were under long-term agreements of typically three to five years that fix commitment, pricing and commodity cost sharing
About 1,500 independent distributor and dealer locations; service parts and related products sell into the installed base
Direct materials about 65%, overhead about 29% and direct labour about 6% of cost of sales; purchased components are about 65% of cost of sales
Price increases of 39 added to Allison Transmission gross profit in the third quarter, with commodity pass-through only for part of the base through long-term agreements
Indianapolis manufacturing of 2.3 million square feet in five plants, plus Chennai, Szentgotthard, Auburn Hills and Lewisburg; about 46 manufacturing and assembly plants acquired
About 4,000 employees (87% in the U.S.) before the acquisition and about 8,000 acquired on 2026-01-01; 49% of legacy U.S. employees and about 68% of acquired U.S. employees are union-represented
Legacy North American truck production is higher in the first half; the issuer calls the third quarter the softest for Allison Off-Highway because of European holidays
Medium-duty and Class 8 vocational truck demand accelerating; Off-Highway mining robust and construction and material handling growing in all regions; industrial and agriculture subdued

runs.text: The main strength is a legacy franchise that earns a 37.47% adjusted EBITDA margin under long-term OEM agreements and converted USD 662 million of free cash flow in nine months, which funds interest and debt repayment. A second strength is liquidity of USD 1,493 million with only USD 320 million of debt due through 2027, which removes near-term refinancing pressure. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation MG-5; calculation FC-1; calculation LQ-1; calculation LQ-3

The main weakness is higher leverage and thinner cover, 3.31x and 6.55x, which leave less room for a truck downturn. A second weakness is the lower-margin Off-Highway business, 45.10% of sales at a 14.03% margin, whose goodwill and intangibles of USD 1,645 million are exposed to impairment if earnings disappoint. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 8; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation LV-1; calculation CV-1; calculation MG-6; calculation MG-9; calculation CS-8

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Allison Transmission Holdings completed the purchase of Dana Incorporated's off-highway business on 2026-01-01 under a stock purchase agreement signed on 2025-06-11. The final price was USD 2,628 million: USD 2,664 million of cash was transferred at closing, USD 2 million of it settling an existing payable, and a USD 34 million post-closing adjustment came back. The annual report gave approximately USD 2,732 million and no source bridges the USD 104 million difference. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 117–118; calculation FD-4; calculation FD-5

The purchase was funded with new debt and cash. Allison Transmission, Inc. issued USD 500 million of senior unsecured notes due December 2033 in November 2025. On 2026-01-02 it added a USD 1,200 million secured incremental term loan due 2033-01-02 at Term SOFR plus 1.75% (5.54% all-in at 2026-09-30), raised the revolver commitments from USD 750 million to USD 1,000 million with a January 2031 maturity and drew USD 300 million. A 364-day bridge commitment of up to USD 2,000 million, cut to USD 500 million by year-end 2025, was never drawn and ended at closing, and cash on hand covered the rest, falling from USD 1,495 million to USD 263 million. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 65; 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 67; 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 118; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation FD-1; calculation FD-6

Since closing the issuer has repaid the revolver draw in full, redeemed USD 100 million of the 2027 notes in September 2026 and cut the Term Loan margin by 0.25% in June 2026. Interest on the new debt cost USD 24 million in the third quarter alone, USD 17 million on the incremental term loan and USD 7 million on the 2033 notes. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; EX-99.1_2026-08-03_d95413dex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation CR-4

Debt fell by USD 255 million over the last two of those quarters while last-twelve-months reported EBITDA rose from USD 1,009 million to USD 1,211 million as acquired quarters replaced pre-closing ones, so part of the improvement is arithmetic and continues only if the acquired business keeps earning at the 2026 rate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cover is the pressure point. EBITDA to cash interest paid was 8.50x in FY2025 and 6.55x over the last twelve months, and net interest expense of USD 51 million in Q3 alone annualises to USD 204 million, which would put run-rate cover at 5.94x on reported-basis EBITDA and 7.01x on adjusted EBITDA. Floating-rate term debt of USD 1,699 million carries the rate exposure, and the twelve-month cash interest figure still includes a quarter before the acquisition debt was drawn.

fields.value: Free cash flow of USD 662 million in the nine months, 65.74% of reported EBITDA, covered USD 410 million of debt repayment and USD 195 million returned to shareholders; the twelve-month figure is USD 831 million. Cash generation is therefore the deleveraging engine, so a working-capital reversal or faster buybacks would slow it.

fields.value: Liquidity at 2026-09-30 is USD 1,493 million, made up of USD 497 million of cash and USD 996 million of undrawn revolver commitments, against USD 4 million of debt due in the rest of 2026 and USD 316 million in 2027. Most of the cash is offshore: USD 361 million, or 72.64%, is held by foreign subsidiaries, so domestic cash is about USD 136 million and the cushion available in the United States is the revolver, which matures in January 2031.

fields.value: Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,166 million in the nine months is USD 159 million, or 13.64%, above reported-basis EBITDA of USD 1,007 million. Most of the gap is purchase accounting (USD 64 million of inventory step-up) and acquisition costs (USD 30 million), but the issuer states no realisation status for any add-back and defines the Other line of USD 7 million by an agreement that is not supplied, so adjusted measures are shown beside the reported basis, not in place of it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Mix dilutes margins. Allison Off-Highway earned a nine-month adjusted EBITDA margin of 14.03% against 37.47% for Allison Transmission, and the consolidated margin fell to 25.88% from 38.06% a year earlier, so coverage now rests partly on a lower-margin business whose agriculture and industrial end markets the issuer calls subdued. Allison Transmission's own net sales rose 8.84%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The acquisition closed on 2026-01-01 and its financing, a USD 1,200 million incremental term loan and a USD 300 million revolver draw, is dated 2026-01-02, both after the 2025-12-31 balance sheet. Year-end 2025 net debt of USD 1,395 million (1.37x) is therefore not a guide to current leverage, and no event after 2026-09-30 changes net debt in the sources read.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer-funded float is small: deferred revenue was USD 179 million at 2026-09-30, mostly extended transmission coverage, against USD 4,012 million of debt, and no supplier finance or receivables sale programme appears in the filings read.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 25; calculation DF-1; calculation TD-5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case that leverage is lower than it looks: the reported-basis ratio uses a twelve-month period that includes a quarter before the acquired business, net debt is 2.46x adjusted EBITDA, and the first lien net leverage ratio the issuer reports is 0.84x against a 5.50x maximum. If the acquired business sustains its nine-month margin and free cash flow stays near USD 662 million for nine months, leverage on a full-year basis would fall faster than the last-twelve-months ratios show.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view turns more cautious on an Off-Highway margin below the 14.03% earned in the nine months, a redraw of the revolver or repayment slower than the USD 255 million of debt reduction over the last two quarters, buybacks above free cash flow, or cash interest running at the annualised USD 204 million rather than the last-twelve-months USD 185 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The purchase was funded almost entirely with new debt, and the new money is mostly secured, which moves existing noteholders further back. New principal of USD 2,000 million (a USD 1,200 million incremental term loan, USD 500 million of unsecured notes and a USD 300 million revolver draw) covered all but USD 628 million of the price, and cash fell from USD 1,495 million at year-end 2025 to USD 263 million after closing. Secured term debt rose by USD 1,190 million to USD 1,699 million, against USD 2,300 million of unsecured notes, so noteholders now sit behind a much larger secured tranche.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Diversification is real but of lower quality than the legacy franchise. Off-Highway is 45.10% of nine-month net sales, spread across construction and material handling at 34.84%, agriculture at 21.46%, industrial at 13.83%, mining at 7.73% and service parts, specialty and other at 22.15%, but it earns an adjusted EBITDA margin of 14.03% against 37.47% for Allison Transmission, and the issuer calls agriculture and industrial demand subdued. Implied pro forma sales growth was 4.15% in the third quarter and 7.57% in the nine months, so the acquisition has not yet shown strong underlying growth.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The legacy business is the anchor of the credit. Allison Transmission net sales rose 8.84% in the nine months, defense sales rose 44.33%, and North American on-highway is 51.21% of segment sales under long-term agreements that cover over 90% of its unit volume. That strength comes with concentration: the top three OEM customers were 39% of 2025 net sales and the top five about 52%, so the loss of one customer or a turn in the truck cycle would hit cash flow directly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management has repaid debt while still returning cash: USD 410 million of debt was repaid in the nine months against USD 195 million returned to shareholders, the dividend was raised for the seventh consecutive year and USD 1,068 million of buyback authority remains. The stated net leverage target of 2.0x has no definition or date, so creditors cannot hold management to a timetable, which is the main reason governance risk is rated Medium rather than Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: There is no sponsor, so the usual extraction routes (dividend recapitalisations, monitoring fees, sponsor-led amendments) are not documented. Ownership is widely dispersed among public holders and one person is Chair, President and Chief Executive Officer, but the proxy statement that would show five-percent holders, board independence and committees and related-party dealings is not supplied. The absence of a sponsor removes one risk and leaves board control unassessed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Integration costs are front-loaded. The issuer guides about USD 125 million of one-time pre-tax expense for 2026, including about USD 65 million of inventory step-up, booked a USD 17 million restructuring charge in the third quarter, and carries goodwill and intangibles of USD 1,645 million, 62.60% of the price, on a preliminary basis. If Off-Highway margins stay near 14.03% that balance becomes an impairment question, and the USD 29 million write-down of electrified-product assets in 2025 shows the issuer has taken such charges before.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Subsequent events are kept out of period figures. The acquisition closed on 2026-01-01 and the term loan and revolver draw are dated 2026-01-02, after the 2025-12-31 balance sheet, so annual report figures describe the company before the purchase, and nothing in the sources read changes the picture after 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view that the diversification is of lower quality could be too harsh: Off-Highway has only three quarters in the numbers, the issuer says construction and mining demand is rebounding from trough levels and the third quarter is seasonally the softest, and the legacy business is at record sales with a 37.47% margin. If integration lifts the Off-Highway margin toward the legacy level, group cash generation would be stronger than the nine-month figures show.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view turns more cautious if the Off-Highway margin stays near 14.03%, if buybacks exceed free cash flow, if the revolver is drawn again, if further debt-funded acquisitions follow, or if the executed debt documents permit large restricted payments or additional priming debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Allison Transmission Holdings completed the purchase of Dana Incorporated's off-highway business on 2026-01-01 under a stock purchase agreement signed on 2025-06-11. The final price was USD 2,628 million: USD 2,664 million of cash was transferred at closing, USD 2 million of it settling an existing payable, and a USD 34 million post-closing adjustment came back. The annual report gave approximately USD 2,732 million and no source bridges the USD 104 million difference.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The purchase was funded with new debt and cash. Allison Transmission, Inc. issued USD 500 million of senior unsecured notes due December 2033 in November 2025. On 2026-01-02 it added a USD 1,200 million secured incremental term loan due 2033-01-02 at Term SOFR plus 1.75% (5.54% all-in at 2026-09-30), raised the revolver commitments from USD 750 million to USD 1,000 million with a January 2031 maturity and drew USD 300 million. A 364-day bridge commitment of up to USD 2,000 million, cut to USD 500 million by year-end 2025, was never drawn and ended at closing, and cash on hand covered the rest, falling from USD 1,495 million to USD 263 million.

fields.value: Since closing the issuer has repaid the revolver draw in full, redeemed USD 100 million of the 2027 notes in September 2026 and cut the Term Loan margin by 0.25% in June 2026. Interest on the new debt cost USD 24 million in the third quarter alone, USD 17 million on the incremental term loan and USD 7 million on the 2033 notes.

fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. Countervailing evidence is the voluntary repayment of USD 410 million, a fully repaid revolver and the absence of a sponsor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Issuer: Allison Transmission Holdings Inc (issuer id alsn), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot. Scope: the fundamental credit view, built from the seven supplied filings and releases and the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance handoffs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Allison's credit profile is adequate but weaker than before the Off-Highway purchase: a high-margin transmission franchise generates the cash to reduce acquisition debt, so creditors are exposed mainly to cycle and integration risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation FC-1; calculation MG-5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On a reported basis total debt is 3.31x EBITDA and cash interest cover is 6.55x, against 2.83x and 8.50x at year-end 2025, and both are distorted by a last-twelve-months period that includes a quarter before the acquisition. Free cash flow of USD 662 million in nine months and liquidity of USD 1,493 million leave room to keep repaying debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation LV-1; calculation LV-2; calculation CV-1; calculation CV-2; calculation FC-1; calculation LQ-1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The primary downside is a North American truck downturn that coincides with weak agriculture and industrial demand at Off-Highway while buybacks and floating-rate interest continue; pro forma EBITDA, executed debt documents and ownership detail are not supplied, so conviction is limited.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The legacy transmission franchise is the main support and held its margin through a down year. Allison Transmission earned an adjusted EBITDA margin of 37.47% in the nine months, and in 2025 net sales fell 6.67% while adjusted EBITDA fell only 3.00%, lifting the margin from 36.12% to 37.54%. Long-term agreements cover over 90% of North American on-highway unit volume and service parts, support equipment and other sales were 21% of 2025 revenue, so contracted volumes and replacement demand cushion a mild downturn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 80; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation MG-1; calculation MG-2; calculation MG-3; calculation MG-4; calculation MG-5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is higher and the improvement so far is partly arithmetic. Total debt to reported EBITDA was 4.23x at 2026-03-31 and 3.31x at 2026-09-30, against 2.83x at year-end 2025, with debt down USD 255 million over the two quarters and last-twelve-months EBITDA rising as acquired quarters replaced pre-closing ones. On the issuer's adjusted measure net debt is 2.46x EBITDA, so true leverage may be lower than the reported ratio suggests, although no pro forma figure confirms that.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation LV-1; calculation LV-2; calculation LV-3; calculation LV-7; calculation LV-8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cover is the weakest financial metric and will not recover quickly. EBITDA covered cash interest 6.55x over the last twelve months against 8.50x in 2025, and net interest expense of USD 51 million in the third quarter annualises to USD 204 million, which puts run-rate cover at 5.94x. The USD 1,699 million of floating-rate term debt has no swaps, so each 1% rise in rates adds USD 16.99 million of interest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 101; calculation CV-1; calculation CV-2; calculation CV-3; calculation CV-4; calculation CV-6; calculation CV-7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate but thin in the United States, and maturities are distant. Liquidity is USD 1,493 million, but USD 361 million of the USD 497 million of cash is held by foreign subsidiaries, leaving USD 136 million of domestic cash behind the revolver. Only USD 320 million falls due through 2027 and 78.29% of principal matures in 2031 or later, so refinancing is a medium-term rather than a near-term test.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation LQ-1; calculation LQ-2; calculation LQ-3; calculation LQ-4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Noteholders now sit behind more secured debt. Secured term debt rose by USD 1,190 million to USD 1,699 million, 42.49% of principal, ahead of USD 2,300 million of unsecured notes, so the existing notes carry more priority claims while the debt documents that would size collateral and permitted debt are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 101; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation CS-1; calculation CS-2; calculation CS-3; calculation CS-4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Off-Highway is the unproven part of the credit. It earns an adjusted EBITDA margin of 14.03% against 37.47% for Allison Transmission on 45.10% of nine-month sales, implied pro forma sales growth is 7.57%, the issuer calls agriculture and industrial demand subdued, and goodwill and intangibles of USD 1,645 million are 62.60% of the price. Weak margins would slow deleveraging and invite impairment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 8; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation MG-6; calculation MG-9; calculation MG-12; calculation CS-8; calculation CS-9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is the main judgement call. The issuer returned USD 195 million to shareholders in nine months, 29.46% of free cash flow, while repaying USD 410 million of debt, and its net leverage target of 2.0x has no definition or date. Creditors therefore depend on management's discretion for the pace of deleveraging.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for a better view is that the first lien net leverage ratio the issuer reports is 0.84x against a 5.50x maximum, net debt is 2.46x adjusted EBITDA, debt fell by USD 255 million in two quarters, the Moody's and Fitch ratings are unchanged since year-end 2025, and guidance implies fourth-quarter adjusted free cash flow of USD 188 million to USD 238 million. If fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA reaches the USD 414 million top of the implied range and repayments continue, last-twelve-months leverage would fall faster than the pace so far.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation LV-3; calculation LV-8; calculation GD-2; calculation GD-3; calculation GD-4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view turns more cautious if fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA falls to the USD 364 million implied by the low end of guidance, if the Off-Highway margin stays at or below 14.03%, if buybacks rise above free cash flow, or if the revolver is redrawn. It would improve if pro forma EBITDA shows a materially higher combined earnings base or the debt documents prove restrictive on payments to shareholders.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Pro forma EBITDA for the acquired business is not available, so the conclusion that leverage is above year-end levels rests on last-twelve-months ratios; a full-year pro forma figure would probably lower the ratio and move the leverage assessment up toward the issuer's adjusted view of 2.46x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so the conclusion that noteholders have lost priority rests on stated security status and could be reduced or increased by guarantees and collateral terms that are not visible.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 101; calculation CS-2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Ownership detail and board independence are not supplied, so the adequate assessment of financial policy rests on observed repayment and repurchase behaviour and would change if board-level constraints or large holders were identified.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Guidance covers 2026 only and no order backlog is disclosed, so the outlook beyond the next year is judgement and could be wrong in either direction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Allison makes fully automatic transmissions and electric propulsion solutions for commercial vehicles, buses, motorhomes and U.S. defense vehicles, sells service parts and extended coverage through a network of independent distributors and dealers, and since 2026-01-01 also makes drivetrain and motion systems for construction, agriculture, mining, material handling and industrial equipment. The legacy business is cash generative and contractually anchored, while the acquired business broadens end markets at lower margins, so the model supports debt service but with a larger share of cyclical, lower-margin revenue than before.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Allison Transmission Holdings, Inc. is a listed company with no sponsor or controlling holder identified, and its wholly-owned subsidiary Allison Transmission, Inc. borrows and issues the notes. Dispersed ownership removes a sponsor extraction path but the proxy statement that would show large holders, board independence and related-party dealings is not supplied, and no guarantor or subsidiary-level financial information is available, so structural priority cannot be sized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 123; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is cyclical and OEM-driven but contract-supported: North American on-highway is 51.21% of legacy sales, long-term agreements cover over 90% of its unit volume with pricing and commodity cost sharing, and the top five OEM customers were about 52% of 2025 sales. Defense sales rose 44.33% in nine months and price increases added to gross profit, which supports visibility, but concentration means one customer loss or a truck-cycle turn would reduce cash flow quickly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation MG-10; calculation MG-11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are defensible in a mild downturn but exposed to deeper volume losses. Direct materials are about 65% of cost of sales and overhead about 29%, and commodity costs pass through only in part, but the 2025 experience of a 6.67% sales decline with only a 3.00% fall in adjusted EBITDA shows price and cost actions have worked. At Off-Highway, with a 14.03% margin, fixed-cost under-absorption in weak demand would bite harder.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51; 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 59; 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 80; calculation MG-3; calculation MG-4; calculation MG-6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow conversion is high but 2026 carries one-time leakage. Free cash flow was USD 662 million in nine months, 65.74% of reported EBITDA and USD 831 million over the last twelve months, after capital expenditure that the issuer guides at USD 240 million to USD 260 million for 2026 including about USD 20 million one-time, and about USD 60 million of one-time acquisition cash outlays. Conversion is therefore likely to stay supportive for debt service, but integration spend and working capital tied up by the acquisition reduce what is left for repayment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation FC-1; calculation FC-2; calculation FC-3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Rivalry is limited in North American on-highway, where Allison supplies the fully automatic transmission, but vertically integrated OEMs and competitors such as Caterpillar, Komatsu and Volvo cap share in mining and construction, which limits growth at Off-Highway.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - New entrants face high engineering and manufacturing barriers, and fully electric propulsion remains in a developmental phase for medium- and heavy-duty vehicles, so electrification is a long-dated rather than near-term threat to cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Substitutes are manual and automated manual transmissions, mainly in Class 8 line-haul where Allison has limited exposure, so substitution risk is concentrated in a small part of sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Buyer power is high because a handful of OEMs buy most volume, offset by long-term agreements and by end users who often specify the Allison product.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Supplier power matters through aluminium and steel castings and forgings and a direct-material share of about 65% of cost of sales that passes through only in part.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Political and economic factors are material to credit: defense spending and trade protectionism are named risks, defense sales rose 44.33% in nine months, and foreign-currency exposure from the acquisition is partly hedged through cross-currency swaps and forwards. Social and technological factors, mainly electrification, do not appear to be a primary credit driver within the horizon of the provided materials.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Strengths: a 37.47% legacy margin, long-term OEM agreements, a sizeable aftermarket, record legacy sales and USD 1,493 million of liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Weaknesses: leverage of 3.31x on reported EBITDA, interest cover of 6.55x, customer concentration, unhedged floating-rate debt and a lower-margin acquired business.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Opportunities: integration savings and rebounding construction and mining demand at Off-Highway, and continued growth in defense.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Threats: a truck-cycle downturn, subdued agriculture and industrial demand, tariffs and trade policy, and impairment of acquired intangibles.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 10; EX-99.1_2026-08-03_d95413dex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation LV-1; calculation CV-1; calculation MG-5; calculation LQ-1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main strength is a legacy franchise that earns a 37.47% adjusted EBITDA margin under long-term OEM agreements and converted USD 662 million of free cash flow in nine months, which funds interest and debt repayment. A second strength is liquidity of USD 1,493 million with only USD 320 million of debt due through 2027, which removes near-term refinancing pressure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation MG-5; calculation FC-1; calculation LQ-1; calculation LQ-3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main weakness is higher leverage and thinner cover, 3.31x and 6.55x, which leave less room for a truck downturn. A second weakness is the lower-margin Off-Highway business, 45.10% of sales at a 14.03% margin, whose goodwill and intangibles of USD 1,645 million are exposed to impairment if earnings disappoint.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 8; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation LV-1; calculation CV-1; calculation MG-6; calculation MG-9; calculation CS-8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position, and competitive advantage, are assessed as strong because Allison is the largest maker of fully automatic transmissions for its core markets and earns a 37.47% margin. Business diversification, cost and capex flexibility, margin stability, free cash flow stability, the ability to refinance and liquidity are average: the acquisition broadened end markets but at a 14.03% margin, cost actions held margin in 2025, free cash flow is 65.74% of EBITDA, maturities are distant but leverage is 3.31x, and liquidity is USD 1,493 million with thin domestic cash. Financial policy and governance is average because debt is being repaid while USD 195 million was returned to shareholders and the leverage target is undefined. The trend is improving from a peak of 4.23x at 2026-03-31, and the key missing datapoints are pro forma EBITDA, the debt documents and ownership detail.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation LV-1; calculation LV-7; calculation FC-2; calculation FC-5; calculation LQ-1; calculation MG-5; calculation MG-6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the issuer has raised 2026 guidance twice, to net sales of USD 5,975 million to USD 6,075 million, adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,530 million to USD 1,580 million and adjusted free cash flow of USD 850 million to USD 900 million, which implies fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA of USD 364 million to USD 414 million against USD 400 million in the third quarter, so the guidance allows a modest decline or a modest rise. Tailwinds are record legacy sales, defense growth and rebounding construction and mining demand; headwinds are subdued agriculture and industrial demand, integration costs of about USD 125 million of one-time expense and tariffs. Beyond two years no company plan is supplied, so the medium-term view rests on the long-term agreements, the aftermarket and the maturity profile, with electrification a longer-dated risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_d187329dex991.htm.jsonl, page 12; EX-99.1_2026-08-03_d95413dex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-08-03_d95413dex991.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation GD-1; calculation GD-2; calculation GD-3; calculation GD-4; calculation GD-5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer-specific downside begins with a North American truck downturn like 2025, when legacy net sales fell 6.67%, arriving while agriculture and industrial demand stay subdued. The first operational break is volume against a cost base that is about 29% overhead, followed by under-absorption at the acquired plants where the margin is only 14.03%. Financial transmission runs through EBITDA to interest cover, which is already 6.55x on the last twelve months and 5.94x on run-rate interest, with USD 1,699 million of floating-rate debt unhedged and USD 195 million of nine-month shareholder returns continuing unless cut. Management levers are suspending buybacks, trimming capital expenditure and the revolver, with liquidity of USD 1,493 million, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity problem before the USD 300 million 2027 notes fall due, but deleveraging would stall and the observable triggers are a fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA below USD 364 million and an Off-Highway margin below 14.03%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_alsn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_alsn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation MG-3; calculation MG-6; calculation CV-1; calculation CV-4; calculation CV-6; calculation FC-5; calculation GD-1; calculation LQ-1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Allison presents an adequate business profile supported by a high-margin transmission franchise, long-term OEM agreements and a large aftermarket, but credit quality is constrained by acquisition leverage of 3.31x, interest cover of 6.55x and an unproven lower-margin Off-Highway business. Cash-flow durability appears adequate due to free cash flow of USD 662 million in nine months and cost actions that held margin in 2025. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on continued repayment, stable ratings and the 2029 and 2031 maturities. The primary downside path is a North American truck downturn coinciding with weak off-highway demand. Further analysis would require pro forma EBITDA, the executed debt documents and ownership detail. Top risk: a cyclical volume decline that stalls deleveraging while interest and shareholder returns continue.
